h: Castles, Coast and Country Near the Zoo
p: Northumberland Zoo sits just off the A1 north of Morpeth, which makes it an easy stop if you're heading up the coast or just looking for a local outing. Its size is its strength: you can take your time, stop and watch, and fit in a keeper talk or two without feeling rushed. With younger children, that's a real bonus. Bring a picnic if the weather is kind, and pack a waterproof just in case.

The area around Morpeth is one of England's great castle country corners. A short drive north, Warkworth Castle, cared for by English Heritage, stands above a loop of the River Coquet, and the village beneath it is lovely for a wander. Alnwick Castle, home to the Duke of Northumberland, is famous for appearing in the Harry Potter films, and The Alnwick Garden next door has its grand cascade, a poison garden and a huge treehouse.

If you'd prefer the coast, Druridge Bay Country Park has a lake, woodland and a long sandy beach that stretches for miles. Inland, Cragside near Rothbury, run by the National Trust, was the first house in the world lit by hydroelectricity, and its grounds are packed with woodland walks and adventure play. Back in Morpeth, Carlisle Park on the banks of the Wansbeck is home to the William Turner Garden, celebrating the Tudor botanist born in the town. Add a cuppa in one of the town's cafes, and you've got a gentle and varied day out in Northumberland. Bamburgh, further up the coast, is another castle-and-beach classic if you fancy making a weekend of it.
